text:
The Canucks have lost seven in a row in regulation, been outscored 30-14 in that run, and have seven points in 21 games. Our playoff simulations no longer find a path for them. On Friday J.T. Miller came back to Rogers Arena with the Rangers and, as Daily Hive put it, went back to "yelling at Elias Pettersson" during a 5-1 Rangers win. It's been that kind of month. The bright spots are personal: Brock Boeser reached 500 career points on Friday, the eighth Canuck to get there, and has a point in six straight.

What's frustrating for Manny Malhotra's team is that it isn't all deserved. Vancouver is -38 in goal difference on -26.9 expected, the quality of chances, so the play has been bad but the goaltending has made it worse, 15.3 goals allowed above what the shots deserved. Leevi Meriläinen is projected to start again, at 2.6 goals below expected this season. And the play itself is the problem too: 40% of the five-on-five expected goals is the kind of number that doesn't fix itself on a hot week.

Vegas has points in six straight (4-0-2) and lost Friday only in a shootout to a Nashville team that has won seven in a row. Mark Stone sits two points from the top of the franchise's career scoring list. The third line has been the surprise: Victor Olofsson has 10 points in his last eight games, and the chances back it, 3.2 expected goals on his own shots. He is our depth Sleeper tonight at 28% to score, and William Karlsson is our Sleeper for a point at 43%, both because the Canucks give up the second-most expected goals per 60 in the league.

Both teams had a day off. Our numbers have this as the most lopsided game of the night on chances, 3.79 expected goals for Vegas to 2.44. Vegas won the only meeting 3-2 in October, a game it deserved 91% of the time.
headline: Seven straight losses, and Vegas is next for Vancouver
